contracts.name: Neonatal recording context and daily reporting
contracts.definition: Minimum context needed to interpret each 24-hour neonatal continuous video-EEG period and its clinically relevant changes.
contracts.applicability: Every neonatal recording and each reported 24-hour period.
criteria: Record postmenstrual age (PMA) at acquisition; PMA is gestational age from last menstrual period plus chronological age.
Source categories are preterm <37 weeks PMA, term 37 up to 44 weeks PMA, and post-term 44 to 48 weeks PMA; the literal wording overlaps at 44 weeks and does not state whether 48 weeks is inclusive.
Record neuroactive medications and ideally administration times, including sedatives, hypnotics, anxiolytics, anesthetics, and antiseizure drugs.
Record hypothermia depth, duration, and whether spontaneous or induced; record major hemodynamic, respiratory, or cardiorespiratory changes.
Record hours uninterpretable for technical reasons; characterize the first hour, one background hour in each later 24-hour period, and additional epochs after relevant change.
Record seizure onset, burden, resolution, and status epilepticus onset and resolution.
exclusions: A waveform-only example without PMA and recording context cannot satisfy this contract.
engineering_choices: Pending Craig: encode term as the half-open interval [37,44) weeks and post-term as beginning at 44 weeks; the upper 48-week boundary remains unresolved.

contracts.name: Behavioral state and sleep-wake cycling
contracts.definition: State assignment combines EEG and polysomnographic behavior and is interpreted relative to PMA.
contracts.applicability: Neonatal recordings with sufficient EEG, eye, respiratory, movement, and preferably EMG observations.
criteria: A state requires its defining features for >=60 seconds.

Allowed states are awake, active sleep, quiet sleep, transitional sleep, and indeterminate sleep; transitional sleep mixes features of the states on either side, while indeterminate sleep cannot be assigned to active or quiet sleep.
Term awake and active sleep use continuous low-to-medium voltage mixed-frequency activité moyenne; active sleep additionally has closed eyes, REM, irregular respiration, and body movement.
Term quiet sleep has closed eyes, absent REM, little movement, and near term commonly tracé alternant; mature continuous high-voltage slow activity and 10-12 Hz spindles emerge around 46 weeks PMA.

Sleep-wake cycling records orderly alteration among states: term complete sleep-wake cycles are typically 3-4 hours and sleep-only cycles 40-70 minutes; preterm sleep cycles are 30-50 minutes below 35 weeks PMA and 50-65 minutes beyond 35 weeks PMA.
Unspecified state change requires distinct EEG patterns differing in discontinuity, voltage, or frequency, with each state lasting >=60 seconds.
exclusions: Do not force active or quiet sleep when clinical and EEG features are insufficient or discordant.
A short page cannot establish sleep-wake cycling.
measurement_requirements: respiration, movement, and EMG when available

contracts.name: Normal continuity, tracé discontinu, and tracé alternant

source.section: Behavioral state; EEG background - continuity; Figures 1-2; Box 3; Table 1

contracts.definition: Normal neonatal continuity and discontinuity are PMA- and state-dependent rather than fixed adult categories.
contracts.applicability: Background assessment in preterm, term, and post-term neonates.
criteria: Continuous activity has no interruption and <2 seconds of attenuation below 25 µV peak-to-peak.
An interburst interval (IBI) is attenuation below an age-dependent level described broadly as <25-50 µV peak-to-peak for >=2 seconds; Table 1 supplies the age bins.
Normal maximum IBI/voltage by PMA: <30 weeks, 35 seconds and <25 µV; 30-33 weeks, 20 seconds and <25 µV; 34-36 weeks, 10 seconds and approximately 25 µV; 37-40 weeks, 6 seconds and >25 µV.

Tracé discontinu contains 50-300 µV bursts with low-voltage IBIs and age-appropriate graphoelements; it is developmentally expected mainly from 26-40 weeks PMA and becomes confined to quiet sleep with maturation.

Tracé alternant occurs only in quiet sleep: 50-150 µV delta bursts lasting roughly 4-10 seconds alternate with 25-50 µV mixed theta-delta periods that never fall below 25 µV; it appears around 34-36 weeks, is minimal by 42 weeks, and is absent by 46 weeks PMA.
exclusions: Do not label age-appropriate discontinuity excessive using a fixed IBI threshold.
The source gives no Table 1 normal IBI row above 40 weeks PMA.

contracts.name: Excessive discontinuity and neonatal burst suppression

source.section: EEG background - excessive background discontinuity; burst suppression; Figures 1-2; Box 3

contracts.definition: Separates PMA-inappropriate discontinuity that retains normal elements from invariant burst suppression lacking normal graphoelements.
contracts.applicability: Discontinuous neonatal backgrounds assessed against PMA and state.
criteria: Excessive discontinuity has IBIs too long or too voltage-depressed for PMA while bursts retain some age-appropriate patterns or graphoelements.
Burst suppression has invariant abnormal bursts separated by prolonged IBIs with voltage <5 µV peak-to-peak.

Permitted activity within burst-suppression IBIs is limited to sparse activity up to 15 µV in one electrode, transient activity up to 15 µV for <2 seconds, or the source-described >2:1 voltage asymmetry in multiple electrodes.

Burst suppression is unreactive and lacks spontaneous lability; bursts lack recognizable normal graphoelements and should be described as >100 µV or <100 µV, with typical burst and IBI durations and burst-component sharpness recorded.
exclusions: Do not call a variable or reactive record with normal graphoelements burst suppression.
Do not infer severity from discontinuity without PMA and state.

contracts.name: Background symmetry and interhemispheric synchrony
contracts.definition: Symmetry compares homologous content and voltage; synchrony compares burst onset timing and has a non-linear developmental course.
contracts.applicability: Multichannel neonatal background, with synchrony assessed during discontinuous portions.
criteria: Persistent >2:1 voltage difference between homologous regions, or persistent disparity in frequency or graphoelement distribution, is abnormal asymmetry; fleeting differences may remain normal.
A burst pair is synchronous when left and right onsets differ by <=1.5 seconds; report the percentage of synchronous bursts.
Near-complete synchrony is expected before roughly 27-29 weeks and again near term; about 70% synchrony may occur around 29-30 weeks and some asynchrony is expected from 30-37 weeks.
After 38 weeks PMA, substantial asynchrony is not expected; abnormal asynchrony means a clearly excessive PMA-adjusted proportion of bursts with onset difference >1.5 seconds.
exclusions: Synchrony does not describe continuous portions without identifiable bursts.
No universal abnormal percentage cutoff is supplied; judgment remains PMA-conditioned.

contracts.name: Term background voltage and electrocerebral inactivity

source.section: EEG background - voltage; electrocerebral inactivity; Figure 1; Box 3

contracts.definition: Voltage categories for term neonatal background plus the separately standardized technical claim of electrocerebral inactivity (ECI).
contracts.applicability: Voltage categories apply primarily to term infants; ECI requires a recording performed to separate ECI technical standards.
criteria: Normal term background has most activity >=25 µV peak-to-peak in every behavioral state.
Borderline low voltage is continuous, retains normal activity and graphoelements, and is persistently >=10 and <25 µV peak-to-peak.
Low-voltage suppressed background lacks normal features, has fundamental baseline <10 µV peak-to-peak, permits >=10 µV transients only when <2 seconds, and is invariant and unreactive.

ECI means no discernible cerebral activity at or above 2 µV peak-to-peak when reviewed at sensitivity 2 µV/mm and only when ECI technical standards were met; otherwise report only that the record may be consistent with ECI.
exclusions: The source declines to define normal voltage limits for premature infants.
Do not determine cerebral death from this EEG term alone.
Do not apply ECI after a standard neonatal acquisition that lacks ECI technical requirements.

contracts.name: Background variability and reactivity
contracts.definition: Variability is spontaneous change from internal state; reactivity is cerebral EEG change after external stimulation.
contracts.applicability: Neonatal background with sufficient longitudinal state sampling and documented stimulation.
criteria: A qualifying response is a conspicuous change in frequency, continuity, or voltage.
Record each feature as yes, no, or unclear/unknown/not applicable.
Variability first appears near 25 weeks PMA, increases by 28 weeks, and is well established around 30-31 weeks.
Reactivity first appears around 30-32 weeks PMA; record stimulus type and strength.
Separate cerebral change from movement, EMG, crying, and respiratory artifacts; arousal-related voltage attenuation is not automatically discontinuity.
exclusions: Behavioral or muscle response alone is not cerebral EEG reactivity.
Absence during one short state sample does not establish global absence.

contracts.name: EEG dysmaturity
contracts.definition: The EEG background appears developmentally appropriate for an infant at least two weeks younger than the actual PMA.
contracts.applicability: Serial or sufficiently comprehensive neonatal recordings with an assigned EEG maturational age.
criteria: Difference between actual PMA and EEG-implied PMA is >=2 weeks.
Persistent dysmaturity is abnormal; the source frames the concept longitudinally.
exclusions: Do not infer dysmaturity from one isolated feature without an overall maturational assessment.
measurement_requirements: EEG-implied PMA based on state, continuity, synchrony, and graphoelements
serial context when persistence is claimed

contracts.name: Normal neonatal graphoelements
contracts.definition: Named developmental background hallmarks whose morphology, state, distribution, and expected PMA window jointly determine normality.
contracts.applicability: Neonatal background interpreted with PMA and state.
criteria: Monorhythmic delta: 24-34 weeks PMA, up to 200 µV peak-to-peak, stereotyped delta usually occipital, temporal, or central and rarely frontal; typically symmetric, synchronous, and often surface positive.

Delta brushes: most prominent 24-36 weeks, 0.3-1.5 Hz slow waves at 50-250 µV with superimposed 8-12 or 18-22 Hz activity; peak expression 32-34 weeks, with state distribution changing by PMA and occasional quiet-sleep occurrence through 40 weeks.

Rhythmic temporal theta: 24-34 weeks, 25-120 µV theta in approximately 2-second temporal bursts, typically symmetric and maximal at 29-32 weeks; similar activity may occur at vertex or occipital sites.
Anterior dysrhythmia: 32-44 weeks, 50-100 µV frontal delta waves singly or in brief runs, typically symmetric and synchronous.

Encoches frontales: 34-44 weeks, 50-100 µV broad diphasic frontal transients lasting 0.5-0.75 seconds with small initial negative and larger positive phase; typically symmetric/synchronous and enriched during transition from active to quiet sleep.
exclusions: A named morphology outside its PMA/state/distribution context is not automatically a normal graphoelement.
The source states that its list is not exhaustive.

contracts.name: Neonatal sharp-wave transients

source.section: EEG transient patterns - sharp wave transients; Box 5; Figures 3b-3c

contracts.definition: Distinct positive or negative transients are classified using baseline duration, abundance, spatial distribution, repetition, PMA, and background context.
contracts.applicability: Transient assessment in the most continuous portions of neonatal EEG, preferably wakefulness or active sleep.
criteria: A spike lasts <100 ms at baseline; a sharp wave lasts 100-200 ms; the transient must stand apart from background rather than be only sharply contoured background.

Physiologic negative sharp waves are usually 100-200 ms, solitary, symmetric, and mid-temporal/central/centro-temporal against a PMA-normal background; frontal, vertex, and occipital locations are uncommon.

Abnormal negative transients are supported by abnormal background, concentration in one region or hemisphere, atypical location, high abundance, or repetitive runs; source-cited outcome data call rates >11/hour preterm and >13/hour term abnormal.

Positive Rolandic/vertex sharp waves are centered at C3/C4 or vertex with adjacent field; excessive positive mid-temporal waves can indicate focal pathology, while cited upper normal observations are 3/hour preterm and 1.5/hour term.
exclusions: Do not count fleeting sharp contour embedded in discontinuous bursts as a distinct transient.
Abundance boundaries remain debated and the cited rates are not presented as a complete standalone diagnostic rule.
measurement_requirements: 15 mm/s display context or equivalent calibrated time

contracts.name: Brief rhythmic discharge

source.section: EEG transient patterns - brief rhythmic discharges; Box 5

contracts.definition: An evolving rhythmic neonatal discharge resembling seizure activity but lasting less than ten seconds.
contracts.applicability: Neonatal evolving rhythmic events below seizure duration.
criteria: Rhythmic electrical activity shows evolution and duration <10 seconds.
Record accompanying background abnormality and confirmed seizures; these are common contexts but not stated as mandatory criteria.
exclusions: An event lasting >=10 seconds may meet neonatal seizure criteria instead.
A very brief rhythmic pattern without evolution belongs with non-seizure rhythmic/periodic patterns, not BRD.
measurement_requirements: evolution in frequency, voltage, morphology, or location

contracts.name: Neonatal seizure type, electrographic definition, and spread

source.section: Seizures and status epilepticus - neonatal seizures; Box 6

contracts.definition: A neonatal electrographic seizure is a sudden abnormal repetitive evolving EEG event meeting voltage and duration thresholds; clinical coupling is classified separately.
contracts.applicability: Neonatal EEG events with calibrated voltage, continuous duration, evolution, and clinical/video correlation when a clinical class is assigned.
criteria: Electrographic seizure is repetitive and unequivocally evolves in frequency, voltage, morphology, or location, reaches >=2 µV peak-to-peak, and lasts >=10 seconds; there is no minimum electrical frequency.
The 2 µV threshold marks seizure beginning and end; two events are separate only when the inter-event interval is >=10 seconds.
Electroclinical seizure has definite simultaneous clinical seizure signs; electrographic-only seizure has no specific visible clinical sign; clinical-only events have no simultaneous EEG seizure.

Spread classes are diffuse asynchronous involvement of all electrodes, bilateral independent, migrating between hemispheres, lateralized within one hemisphere, unifocal onset, or multifocal onset from >=3 independent foci with >=1 in each hemisphere.
Restricted locations may be frontal, central, temporal, occipital, vertex, anterior quadrant, posterior quadrant, or hemispheric left/right.
exclusions: Do not call evolving activity <10 seconds a seizure; use BRD.
Do not call repetitive activity without evolution a seizure even when >10 seconds.
Do not confuse arousal or drowsiness background transitions with seizures.
Do not use generalized synchronous terminology where the neonatal source specifies diffuse asynchronous spread.

contracts.name: Neonatal seizure burden and status epilepticus
contracts.definition: Seizure burden is quantified over an explicit denominator; neonatal status is defined by seizure occupancy of a one-hour epoch.
contracts.applicability: Continuous neonatal EEG with complete seizure start/stop annotations and a defined analysis epoch.
criteria: Clinical burden may be reported as seizure count per hour or total seizure duration divided by the duration of the epoch of interest.

Research temporal-spatial burden sums seizure duration per hour in five non-overlapping neonatal montage regions so each electrode is counted once; the source lists Fp3-T3, C3-O1, Fp4-T4, C4-O2, Fz-Pz or an alternate pairing.
Status epilepticus is present when summed seizure duration is >=50% of any defined 60-minute epoch.
exclusions: Do not report a percentage without the epoch denominator.
The source explicitly describes the 50% status cutoff as somewhat arbitrary rather than outcome-validated.
measurement_requirements: non-overlapping region mapping for spatial burden

contracts.name: Neonatal rhythmic and periodic patterns of uncertain significance

source.section: Rhythmic and periodic patterns - patterns, duration, location; Figure 3c; Box 7

contracts.definition: Non-seizure periodic discharges and rhythmic delta activity are described by waveform organization, minimum cycles, onset, spread, and neonatal location terms.
contracts.applicability: Neonatal rhythmic or periodic patterns that do not have seizure-defining evolution.
criteria: Periodic discharges have relatively uniform morphology/duration, a measurable interdischarge interval, and near-regular recurrence: cycle length varies <50% between adjacent cycles in >50% of cycle pairs.
A discharge has <=3 phases or lasts <=0.5 seconds regardless of phases; a burst lasts >0.5 seconds and has >=4 phases.
RDA repeats relatively uniform waveforms without an inter-wave interval and has cycle-length variation <50% in >50% of adjacent cycle pairs.
PD or RDA must persist for >=6 cycles.

Location is lateralized, diffuse with asynchronous all-electrode involvement, bilateral independent, or multifocal; report onset focus, maximal spread, and F/C/T/O/Z or hemispheric predominance as applicable.
For diffuse patterns, frontal, occipital, or midline predominance requires amplitude >=50% greater than the comparison region in an appropriate referential montage.
exclusions: Evolution is not an RPP modifier in neonates because evolution defines BRD or seizure according to duration.
Neonatal RDA is not necessarily abnormal; normal rhythmic occipital delta and anterior dysrhythmia can meet rhythmic form.

contracts.name: Neonatal rhythmic/periodic duration, polarity, and sharpness modifiers

source.section: Rhythmic and periodic patterns - modifiers; Box 7

contracts.definition: Neonatal RPPs use a limited modifier set with neonatal duration boundaries and bipolar polarity measurement.
contracts.applicability: Non-continuous neonatal PD/RDA patterns; polarity and sharpness apply only to PDs and the spike/sharp component of spike-wave patterns, not RDA.
criteria: Record typical duration and preferably longest continuous duration: very long >=1 hour; long 5-59 minutes; intermediate 1-4.9 minutes; brief 10-59 seconds; very brief <10 seconds without evolution.
Determine predominant-phase polarity in a traditional bipolar montage as positive, negative, or unclear.

Measure sharpness at baseline for predominant and sharpest phase: spiky <100 ms; sharp 100-200 ms; sharply contoured theta/delta is >200 ms with steep or pointed morphology; blunt is smooth or sinusoidal.
exclusions: Do not apply polarity or sharpness to RDA.
Do not use the newer non-neonatal 10-59 minute long-duration boundary; S09 specifies 5-59 minutes.
Very brief evolving events are BRDs, not static RPP duration examples.

unresolved_source_ambiguities.issue: The source says term is 37 up to 44 weeks PMA and post-term is 44 to 48 weeks PMA, creating a literal boundary overlap at 44; inclusivity at 48 is unstated.
unresolved_source_ambiguities.current_handling: Literal source wording remains in criteria; a half-open representation is recorded only as an engineering choice pending Craig.

unresolved_source_ambiguities.issue: The prose defines an IBI using attenuation below a broad 25-50 µV peak-to-peak range, while Table 1 gives PMA-specific values of <25, approximately 25, and >25 µV.
unresolved_source_ambiguities.current_handling: Both the prose range and the literal Table 1 values are retained without collapsing them to one cutoff.

unresolved_source_ambiguities.issue: Table 1 stops at 37-40 weeks PMA and supplies no normal maximum IBI row above 40 weeks.
unresolved_source_ambiguities.current_handling: No value above 40 weeks is inferred.

unresolved_source_ambiguities.issue: The burst-suppression paragraph lists >2:1 voltage asymmetry in multiple electrodes alongside permitted sparse/transient IBI activity without clearly stating the logical relationship of that asymmetry clause.
unresolved_source_ambiguities.current_handling: The clause is identified as source-described and is not converted into a stricter logical rule.

unresolved_source_ambiguities.issue: The source explicitly declines to define normal voltage boundaries for premature infants.
unresolved_source_ambiguities.current_handling: Term voltage thresholds are not generalized to preterm infants.

unresolved_source_ambiguities.issue: The source states that physiologic/pathologic sharp-transient boundaries remain debated; its >11/hour preterm, >13/hour term, 3/hour preterm, and 1.5/hour term values are literature observations rather than a complete standalone classification rule.
unresolved_source_ambiguities.current_handling: Rates are retained as contextual supportive thresholds with the uncertainty stated.

unresolved_source_ambiguities.issue: The source defines neonatal status as seizure occupancy >=50% of a one-hour epoch but explicitly calls the cutoff somewhat arbitrary and not specifically justified over another percentage.
unresolved_source_ambiguities.current_handling: The operational cutoff and its evidentiary limitation are both retained.

unresolved_source_ambiguities.issue: The official source PDF visibly contains unresolved author comment balloons questioning the low-voltage-suppressed threshold and requesting a reliability reference for temporal-spatial seizure burden.
unresolved_source_ambiguities.current_handling: Contracts follow the body text; comment-balloon suggestions are not adopted as definitions.
